issues.legal_issue: A former member of the armed forces who becomes landlord of premises only after retirement cannot use the special eviction remedy for those premises.
material_facts: The landlord retired from the armed forces before acquiring the premises.
The premises were gifted to the landlord after retirement, and the tenant had occupied them for years.
The landlord sought possession under the special remedy for armed-forces landlords and produced the required service certificate.
issues.conclusion: The landlord was not entitled to recover possession under the special remedy because he had not been landlord of the premises while serving in the armed forces.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13A1(a) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, read in light of its purpose, benefits armed-forces landlords who leased out premises while in service; they may invoke the remedy during service or after retirement. To avoid an overbroad construction that could expose the provision to an Article 14 challenge, the provision must be read down accordingly. Sushila Bai Vasudev Jaeel v. M. S. Dhillon and Jyotish Ranjan Chakrabarti v. N. K. Mitra were approved; Nihal Chand v. Kalyan Chand and B. N. Mutto v. T. K. Nandi were distinguished. The Court expressed no opinion on a person who becomes landlord while still serving by acquiring title to premises already occupied by a tenant through inheritance, partition, transfer or otherwise.

rule.if: special_eviction_case and claimant_former_service_member and claimant_acquired_premises_after_retirement and not landlord_during_service

predicates.special_eviction_case: The proceeding seeks possession of rented premises through a special eviction remedy for armed-forces landlords.
predicates.claimant_former_service_member: The claimant previously served as a member of the armed forces.
predicates.claimant_acquired_premises_after_retirem: The claimant acquired the premises after retiring from armed-forces service.
predicates.landlord_during_service: The claimant was landlord of the premises while serving in the armed forces.

issues.definition: When a former service member seeks possession through the special eviction remedy, acquiring the premises only after retirement and not being their landlord during service means the special entitlement is absent.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord cannot obtain eviction on the ordinary bona fide requirement ground without establishing a genuine need for the premises.
material_facts: The landlord also relied on the ordinary statutory ground of bona fide requirement.
The High Court found that the landlord had not established a genuine need for the premises.
The Supreme Court agreed with that finding while considering the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The landlord was not entitled to eviction under section 13(1)(g) because genuine need had not been established.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 13(1)(g) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, the landlord's bona fide requirement must be established. The Court upheld the High Court's finding that the evidence did not establish genuine need.

predicates.ordinary_bona_fide_requirement_case: The proceeding seeks eviction on the ground that the landlord bona fide requires the premises.
predicates.landlord_failed_to_establish_genuine_nee: The landlord did not establish a genuine need for the premises.

issues.definition: In a proceeding based on a landlord's claimed bona fide requirement, failure to establish genuine need means ordinary eviction relief is unavailable.
